approval.cost: The docs read state no developer fee, review fee, or revenue share. Plan gating is a cost in kind: 'API access is only available to active Egnyte customers on eligible plans. Egnyte domains on Trial, Legacy Office, or Team plans are not supported'
approval.trigger: Egnyte approval is required, twice over. (1) Key activation: 'When you create the key the status would be Pending Approval and after verification of the request, the status will change to Active', depending on prerequisites (eligible plan, domain-admin requester, valid admin email). (2) Production approval of the completed app: 'initially your API key will only work with the single Egnyte domain you told us you would use for testing. When we approve your completed app, we will remove the domain restriction from the key so that it works with any Egnyte domain' (the code-exchange section adds: 'we will issue you a new key that works with any Egnyte domain'). Scope discipline is an explicit approval criterion: 'all third party applications must scope token requests to only the endpoints they need. We will not approve applications for production use unless they properly scope their token requests or demonstrate a valid need for global scope.' Pre-approval cap: your key works against ONE test domain only until Egnyte approves the finished app. Each customer domain is also capped: 'The Egnyte domain must not have reached the maximum of 5 API keys'.
approval.wait: Not stated (no duration anywhere in the docs read; approval is described only as a status change after 'verification of the request')

blockers.detail: You cannot test against real customer domains before approval: the key is domain-locked to your test domain, and production approval replaces/unlocks the key ('we will issue you a new key'), so plan a credential cutover.
blockers.howToClear: Build the connection layer to swap keys per domain without re-deploying.
blockers.title: Two-stage, one-way gating with a key cutover

blockers.detail: 'If you registered the wrong key type or need to update your domain, email us at api-support@egnyte.com.' The Internal/Public choice and the domain are effectively one-way doors.
blockers.howToClear: Choose Publicly Available and the correct domain at registration; corrections go through support.
blockers.title: Wrong key type is a support ticket, not a setting

blockers.detail: Keys requested by non-admins 'will be declined', and service-account emails are excluded: every key traces to a named human domain admin, which complicates fully automated onboarding. Non-customers building a public integration must request a free developer domain from Egnyte's Ecosystem team via a form.
blockers.howToClear: Route key requests through a real domain admin; get a developer domain early if you are not an Egnyte customer.
blockers.title: Admin-only issuance

flavor.recommended: A Publicly Available Application on the Egnyte Developer Portal, using the Authorization Code flow
flavor.why: The object is an application registered on the Egnyte Developer Portal, yielding an API key (used as the OAuth client_id) and a client secret. At registration you must declare the app as one of two types: Publicly Available Application ('an integration for other Egnyte customers to use') or Internal Application ('for: own company's internal use, or contracted to create a solution for a single company'). Egnyte's Getting Started guide: 'Public Applications: If you are building an integration for other Egnyte customers to use, use the Authorization Code (most secure) or Implicit Grant flow', and the Authorization Code Flow 'is designed for applications where... You want to act on behalf of a user.' Each end user authorizes on THEIR OWN Egnyte domain (https://<their-domain>.egnyte.com/puboauth/token), clicks 'Allow Access', and your app exchanges the returned code for access + refresh tokens for that domain.

humanMust: Be (or be sponsored by) an Egnyte customer admin: 'API keys are restricted to Egnyte domain administrators... API keys requested by a non-admin will be declined', and the requester's email 'must be associated with an active domain administrator account' (non-customers: request a free developer domain from the Ecosystem team)
Register a developer account on developers.egnyte.com and confirm the email link
Create a New App with the application form (App Name, Description, Egnyte Domain, Registered OAuth Redirect URI, Type Public/Internal, Current User Base, Platform, which APIs)
Complete the app and get final production approval so Egnyte lifts the single-domain restriction
name: Egnyte
nuances: Per-domain everything: tokens are issued per Egnyte domain (the authorize/token hosts are the customer's own subdomain), so a SaaS must collect and store each customer's domain as part of the connection, and the same user in two domains is two separate connections. Token fragility: password change or explicit revocation invalidates tokens immediately; apps 'must be able to deal with 401 authentication failure scenarios' and fall back to the refresh token or full re-authorization.

API usage caps by plan (bounding the connected app in each customer domain): Business/Essentials 2 calls/sec, 1,000/day, 30,000/month; Enterprise Lite/Elite 2/sec, 2,000/day, 60,000/month; Enterprise/Ultimate 2/sec, 4,000/day, 120,000/month. 'Additional calls can be purchased by contacting Egnyte API Support.' Tight defaults (as low as 1,000 calls/day) make polling-style agents impractical on lower tiers.

Platform migration note: 'Egnyte migrated its API management platform from Mashery to Apigee on October 1st, 2025'; legacy Mashery-era keys/accounts had to be re-created, so older third-party setup guides may be stale.

The redirect URI 'must be an HTTPS URL and must match the callback URL configured for your key'. 'You should persist the OAuth tokens (access and refresh) in your application... Treat the tokens with the same degree of care that you would a saved password.'
prerequisites: An Egnyte domain admin behind the key request (or a developer domain from the Ecosystem team)
The Public vs Internal type decision at registration
An HTTPS redirect URI registered on the key

steps.detail: Register a developer account on developers.egnyte.com and confirm the email link. Create a New App and fill the application form: App Name, Description ('the detailed description of the App explaining the use case and implementation plan', required), Egnyte Domain, Registered OAuth Redirect URI, Type (Publicly Available), Current User Base, Platform, and which APIs (Egnyte Collaborate and/or Secure & Govern).

steps.title: Register the application

steps.detail: On save you receive the API key + secret with status 'Pending Approval'; after Egnyte's verification of the request the status changes to 'Active'. The key initially works only with the single test domain you declared.
steps.title: Wait for key activation

steps.detail: Prompt each connecting user for their Egnyte domain; redirect them to https://<domain>.egnyte.com/puboauth/token?client_id=<API Key>&redirect_uri=...&scope=...&response_type=code. The user logs in and clicks 'Allow Access'. Exchange the code via POST to https://<domain>.egnyte.com/puboauth/token with grant_type=authorization_code, client_id, client_secret, redirect_uri, code, and the same scope. Persist both tokens.
steps.title: Run the per-domain authorization code flow

steps.detail: Call https://<domain>.egnyte.com/pubapi/v1/... with Authorization: Bearer. Bearer tokens expire in 30 days (expires_in 2592000); on a 401/expiry 'use the refresh token to obtain a new pair of access and refresh tokens'.
steps.title: Call the API; refresh on 401/expiry

steps.detail: Submit the completed app for Egnyte's production approval (with properly scoped token requests). On approval Egnyte removes the domain restriction / issues a new key that works with any Egnyte domain.
steps.title: Get production approval (domain restriction lifted)

tagline: A real OAuth program with a classic centralized gate: Egnyte must activate your key, then approve your finished app before the key works beyond your single test domain, and least-privilege scoping is an explicit approval condition.
